title: Pifer says Witkoff made eight Moscow trips without visiting Kyiv
description_short: Pifer says Witkoff made eight Moscow trips without visiting Kyiv
description_medium: In an April 29, 2026 Brookings commentary, Steven Pifer wrote that Steve Witkoff had traveled to Moscow eight times since March 2025 without visiting Kyiv. Pifer cited polls in which 70% of Ukrainians did not expect U.S.-brokered talks to succeed and 28% regarded the United States as reliable. His view that U.S. engagement appeared one-sided is an attributed assessment.
prior_description_long: Steven Pifer’s April 29, 2026 Brookings commentary says U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff had traveled to Moscow eight times since March 2025 without visiting Kyiv. Pifer argues that this pattern made U.S. mediation appear one-sided. He also cites polling in which 70% of Ukrainians did not expect U.S.-brokered talks to succeed and 28% considered the United States a reliable partner. These are reported claims and Pifer’s interpretation, not a demonstrated causal relationship between Witkoff’s travel and public opinion. The cited commentary does not reproduce the itinerary records or full polling methodology. The event date for this account is the commentary’s publication date; March 2025 marks the start of the trip-count period.
description_long: Steven Pifer’s April 29, 2026 Brookings commentary says U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff had traveled to Moscow eight times since March 2025 without visiting Kyiv. Pifer argues that this pattern made U.S. mediation appear one-sided. The article frames the contrast against the Biden administration’s stated “nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine” approach and also discusses the August 2025 Trump-Putin meeting in Alaska. Pifer notes that the leaders provided no specifics about an “understanding” referenced after that meeting; the commentary does not establish what, if anything, they agreed. He also cites polling in which 70% of Ukrainians did not expect U.S.-brokered talks to succeed and 28% considered the United States a reliable partner. These are reported claims and Pifer’s interpretation, not a demonstrated causal relationship between Witkoff’s travel and public opinion. The cited commentary does not reproduce the itinerary records or full polling methodology. The event date for this account is the commentary’s publication date; March 2025 marks the start of the trip-count period.

supported_facts: Brookings identifies Steven Pifer and dates the commentary April 29, 2026.
Pifer reports Witkoff traveled to Moscow eight times since March 2025 and had not visited Kyiv.
The commentary contrasts the Trump approach with the Biden administration’s stated “nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine” principle.
The article discusses the August 2025 Trump-Putin meeting and notes neither leader provided specifics about an “understanding” referenced afterward.
Pifer cites the 70% and 28% poll figures and offers the one-sided-engagement assessment.
limits: This is commentary and the one-sided characterization is Pifer’s assessment.
Underlying itinerary records and full polling methodology are not reproduced or linked; the article does not establish travel caused attitudes or reveal the substance of any private agreement.

unsupported_original_claims: That Witkoff’s travel caused falling Ukrainian confidence or independently proves U.S. mediation bias.
That March 2025 is the publication date of the eight-trip account rather than the start of the reported trip-count period.
Unreported itinerary or polling details, or a definitive account of what was agreed at the Alaska meeting.

title: Trump revokes federal-contractor affirmative-action requirements in EO 14173
description_short: Trump revokes federal-contractor affirmative-action requirements in EO 14173
description_medium: Trump signed Executive Order 14173 on January 21, 2025. It revoked Executive Order 11246, which had imposed affirmative-action requirements on federal contractors, and directed agencies to add anti-discrimination-law compliance terms to federal contracts and grants. The text does not abolish every affirmative-action, outreach, admissions or mentoring program at all federally funded institutions.
prior_description_long: President Trump signed Executive Order 14173 on January 21, 2025. The order revoked Executive Order 11246, ending the prior federal-contractor affirmative-action framework after a 90-day transition, and directed agency heads to include terms requiring contractors and grant recipients to comply with applicable federal anti-discrimination laws and certify that they do not operate DEI programs violating those laws. The action changed federal contracting and grant conditions, but it did not automatically abolish all affirmative-action, outreach, pipeline, mentoring or admissions programs at every institution receiving federal funds. The Federal Register text establishes the administration’s directives; it does not show how each agency or recipient implemented them or determine the legality of every affected program.
description_long: President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14173 on January 21, 2025. The order was published in the Federal Register on January 31 and revoked EO 11246, the basis for the federal-contractor affirmative-action framework, while allowing contractors to continue under the prior regulatory scheme for 90 days. It directed the Labor Department’s Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to stop promoting diversity, holding contractors responsible for affirmative action, and allowing or encouraging workforce balancing. The order also told agencies to include terms in each contract or grant award making compliance with federal anti-discrimination laws material to payment and requiring recipients to certify that they do not operate DEI programs violating those laws. Separately, it directed the attorney general and education secretary to issue guidance within 120 days to federally funded schools and higher-education institutions on compliance with the Supreme Court’s Students for Fair Admissions ruling. These provisions state the administration’s directions; the text alone does not establish their implementation or the legality of a particular recipient’s program. EO 14173 did not itself abolish every outreach, pipeline, mentoring, admissions, or affirmative-action program at all federally funded institutions. Nor does the cited text establish outcomes for any particular recipient. The order also preserves exceptions for certain veteran or Randolph-Sheppard preferences and for protected speech.

supported_facts: The order is signed January 21, 2025 and the Federal Register record was published January 31, 2025.
EO 14173 revokes EO 11246 and gives contractors a 90-day transition under the prior regulatory scheme.

The order directs OFCCP to cease specified actions and directs agencies to include terms in each contract or grant award on applicable anti-discrimination-law compliance and certification about DEI programs violating those laws.

The order directs the Attorney General and Education Secretary to issue guidance within 120 days for specified federally funded educational entities concerning Students for Fair Admissions compliance.
The order states exceptions or protections for specified veteran/Randolph-Sheppard preferences and First Amendment-protected speech.
limits: The order is a set of directives; its text does not prove implementation, outcomes for an individual recipient, or the legality of a specific program.
The certification requirement concerns programs promoting DEI that violate applicable federal anti-discrimination laws; it is not a blanket ban on every program.

unsupported_original_claims: That all federally funded institutions were ordered to eliminate every affirmative-action program on January 20.
That EO 14173 automatically ended every outreach, pipeline, mentoring, or admissions program.
That any institution maintaining any diversity initiative automatically lost funding.
exact_evidence_gap: The order directs agency and contract/grant implementation but does not establish institution-wide effects, implementation status, or outcomes for individual recipients. Its certification language concerns DEI programs that violate applicable federal anti-discrimination laws.
